liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bertha** (1 review): Bertha starts with simple drumming and piano before Weir joins in the left channel [9]
- **Loser** (1 review): Source singles out smoking versions of Loser and Scarlet Begonias [8]
- **Playin' In The Band** (1 review): Twenty-minute version features Jerry inspired and impressive interplay between Bobby and Billy [12]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Let It Grow into Dark Star is described as a long, free-form jazz fusion jam [13]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): Reviewer praises the specific sequence of Weather Report Suite, Dark Star, and China Doll [7]
- **Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad** (1 review): Listener claims Not Fade Away into Goin' Down The Road is the best from 1974 [12]
- **Weather Report Suite** (1 review): Source highlights a rare combo of Weather Report Suite, Dark Star, and China Doll [6]

## The recordings

- **gd74-05-14.sbd.murphy.1823.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 184 min; rated 4.41/5 by 70 [1]. Said about its sound: Listener describes the recording as having an amazing sound from the one-drummer era; Reviewer argues the mix is bad if Jerry is weakest or lost by the soundman; Listener on their specific rig finds the show sounds crispy with Jerry hammering away [8][16][17]
- **gd1974-05-14.163764.sbd.miller.patched.sirmick.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 196 min; rated 5/5 by 4 [2]
- **gd1974-05-14.163756.aud.lamarre.vernon.sirmick.flac24**: audience recording; 23 songs; 177 min [4]
- **gd1974-05-14.sbd.miller.114462.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 195 min; rated 4.28/5 by 36 [3]

## Around the show

- Listener notes Jerry, Keith, and Phil were all performing well that night [6]
- Listener, a Montana resident, recalls the band rocking the venue intensely [13]
- Audience member yells for Tie a Yellow Ribbon just before Playin' In The Band [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd74-05-14.sbd.murphy.1823.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Transfer path: MSR to cassette, DAT, CD-R, TAE, SHN via Bob Murphy [1]
- **gd1974-05-14.163764.sbd.miller.patched.sirmick.flac16**: transferred by This is a patched version of shnid 114462; source: Set 1: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat (48k) Set 2: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat (44.1k) [2]. Also: Patched version fixes China Doll tape flip; only Set 1 needed pitch correction [2]
- **gd1974-05-14.163756.aud.lamarre.vernon.sirmick.flac24**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Matt Vernon, SirMick; source: Audience Cassettes (up to El Paso described on j-card as 7th gen and the rest of show 8th gen) from collection of Doug Lamarre [4]. Also: Fades reversed and sections patched from shnid 114462; missing parts from other sources; Despite many tape generations, listener hears little hiss but suspects lower generation [4]
- **gd1974-05-14.sbd.miller.114462.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Set 1: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat (48k) Set 2: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat (44.1k) [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by RareVinyl.com: [Grateful Dead Dave's Picks Volume 9: Harry Adams Field House, U. Of Montana, Missoula, MT 5/14/74 US 3-CD set](https://eu.rarevinyl.com/products/grateful-dead-dave-s-picks-volume-9-harry-adams-field-house-u-of-montana-missoula-mt-5-14-74-us-3-cd-album-triple-set-r2541133-848359) [19]
- Fan art by KINGKONG: [Grateful Dead – Dave's Picks, Volume 9 (Harry Adams Field House, U. Of Montana, Missoula, MT • 5/14/74) ■YMR■ | KINGKONG](https://kkrecords.buyshop.jp/items/70098389) [20]
- Fan art by SoundCloud: [The Grateful Dead's "Wall of Sound" 1974, â® Adams Field House](https://soundcloud.com/masaki-okamuro/sets/the-grateful-deads-wall-of-sound-1974-adams-field-house) [21]
